title.en: The Shungas, Satavahanas, Kharavela and the Indo-Greeks

text.en:
Meena saw coins with Greek faces in a museum.
"Those are Indo-Greek coins," said her teacher.

After the Mauryas the Shungas ruled in the north and supported art, building the railings at the Sanchi stupa. The Satavahanas ruled the Deccan and grew rich through trade with Rome and spread Buddhism and Prakrit literature.
Kharavela of Chedi in Kalinga is known from the Hathigumpha inscription. The Indo-Greeks came from the north-west and issued fine coins with portraits.
This age of new kingdoms mixed cultures and produced great art such as the Sanchi stupa gateways.
